_doc: A farm's ground (#99): wheat is a crop of grain, pooled over the field; reaped bare it's stubble, which the farmer sows again into wheat. Coal, iron and gold seams run through the mountains (#42): a mine against one digs it out, and a dug-out seam is worked-out rock. Trees are one trunk each, and a woodcutter plants saplings that grow into trees (#126).

wheat.note: a farm's wheat: its grain is pooled over its tiles; reaped bare it's stubble till sown again

stubble.note: a reaped field: stubble, waiting for the farmer to sow it again

coal_seam.note: a seam of coal in the mountain: a mine against it digs it out

iron_seam.note: a seam of iron ore in the mountain: a mine against it digs it out

gold_seam.note: a seam of gold ore in the mountain: a mine against it digs it out

worked_out.note: a seam dug out: bare rock

tree.note: a tree in Steading is one trunk: felled in one go and carried home whole (the genre's woodcutter, #126)

sapling.note: a sapling a woodcutter planted: a tree ten minutes on (#126); nothing goes up or through it meanwhile
